thread:
maria: heads-up — seeing a steady rise in GPU slot scarcity this morning. cluster-autoscaler says capacity available but pods are pending because nodes are stuck in 'Draining' for 20-40m. :eyes:

sam: ugh. which regions/nodes? any common taints/labels?

maria: eu-west1 primarily. affected nodes have the 'maintenance/rolling=true' taint but are flip-flopping between cordoned and uncordoned while kubelet tries to evict DaemonSets + local-ssd pods. netlink logs show flaky pod deletions.

jordan: saw similar last week but that was k8s 1.26 kubelet bug with podDeletion backoff. what kubelet version there?

maria: 1.25.8. ops-bot reports repeating drain attempts from autoscaler controller. snippet from the node's kubelet log: 
```
I0321 09:12:46.123456 kubelet.go:224] cordon node-45
E0321 09:12:46.543210 kubelet_eviction.go:98] pod "trainer-0" deletion timed out after 120s
W0321 09:24:46.543211 kubelet_delete.go:147] retrying delete, pod still terminating (grace 0)
```

lee: that's causing the scheduler to treat those GPUs as reserved but not usable — cluster shows 12 GPUs offline. billing still counts them.

sam: is the descheduler kicking in and reassigning pods? or are we getting cordon/un-cordon churn?

maria: both. automation sees drains failing and retries, a bookkeeper job then removes the taint, which lets some pods land, then another maintenance controller re-adds taint. repeat.

ops-bot: automated-evict triggered: node-45 -> 6 pods forced delete (grace 0) at 09:30:12

jordan: forced deletes are making things worse — pods restart and try to re-schedule to the same node and get evicted again. pinging infra on possible network delays to kube-apiserver in eu-west1.

sam: short-term mitigation ideas: 1) increase drain retry interval, 2) reduce concurrent evictions per node (eviction-burst -> 3), 3) add a "drain-lock" annotation on nodes to stop automated undo of cordon.

maria: proposal: roll a canary change to autoscaler/maintenance controller to: 
- set eviction-burst to 3
- annotate nodes with maintenance/locked=true during drain window
- extend kubelet pod deletion timeout from 120s -> 300s on canary hosts

lee: agree on canary. also we should patch our monitoring to alert on cordon/un-cordon frequency (>=3 flips in 10m) so oncall can catch thrash before it starves capacity.

jordan: longer-term: investigate fixing the podDeletion backoff and consider dedicating a tiny reserved pool for high-priority GPU jobs so user-facing workloads don't see immediate capacity loss during volatile drains.

sam: I'll open a quick PR for the maintenance controller canary. command I'll run for canary drains: 
```bash
kubectl annotate node node-45 maintenance/locked=true --overwrite
kubectl drain node-45 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=5m
```

maria: careful with delete-local-data — some training jobs write checkpoints to local SSD, need a label check to skip those nodes.

sam: good call — will add a skip label and a fallback policy to move long-lived local-ssd pods to reserved pool first.

ops-bot: alert: eu-west1 GPU utilization spike -> pending pods 47 -> impacted queues: prod-train, batch-infer

lee: can we do a manual lift for prod-train onto a different pool (non-preemptible) while canary runs? cost hit but reduces customer impact.

maria: yes, we have 8 reserved GPUs in eu-west1 dedicated to high-priority routes. I'll schedule a one-off move of 3 trainers there.

jordan: note for postmortem: include GPU hours wasted, number of forced evictions, and a timeline of cordon/un-cordon flips. we should also attach kubelet logs and maintenance controller logs.

sam: PR link (canary): https://github.com/redwoodinfra/maintenance-controller/pull/842 :eyes: will roll to eu-west1-canary pool first.

maria: thanks — tracking in #incidents and will update ops runbook with a new step: mark node maintenance/locked=true before drain and watch for cordon flips.

lee: oncall will monitor for 2h post-rollout. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: note: automated-evict throttled to 3 concurrent deletes per node (temporary canary)

maria: update 10:45 — canary kicked off, one node drained cleanly, two others still show podDeletion retries. continuing investigation with kubelet debug logs.

sam: if retries keep failing we may need to increase kubelet timeout cluster-wide. opened ticket with infra to check apiserver latency and node network metrics.

maria: TL;DR — root cause likely drain thrash + podDeletion/backoff on kubelet 1.25; mitigation is canary change to throttle evictions, lock drains, and reserve small high-priority pool. will follow up with a brief postmortem after stabilization.
